text: This source describes the so-called Nestor Ring, presented in the article as a disputed Pseudo-Minoan artifact. The 2011 peer-reviewed article examines the circumstances of its 1924 discovery and argues that those circumstances are suspicious. It further argues that the artifact's semantic coherence depends on Egyptian prototypes and that its use of the butterfly motif weighs against authenticity.

This source describes the temporary exhibition “Princes of Pylos. Bronze Age Treasures of Messenia,” focused on grave goods from the Griffin Warrior Tomb and other Bronze Age discoveries in Messenia; it does not specifically discuss the Ring of Nestor’s authenticity, alleged forgery, microscopic engraving, or iconographic interpretation. The article states that approximately 1,400 grave goods accompanied the burial of a 30–35-year-old man in a pit grave dated to 1450 BC, excavated in 2015 near the Palace of Nestor. The exhibition was organized by the Greek Ministry of Culture and the Ephorate of Antiquities of Messenia in collaboration with Jack L. Davis and Sharon Stocker of the University of Cincinnati.

This source describes the Palace of Nestor at Pylos, Greece, rather than the Ring of Nestor itself. It presents the palace as an important Mycenaean centre and the best-preserved Mycenaean Greek palace discovered, with a settlement occupied over a long period, artifacts mostly dating to 1300 BC, and destruction by fire around 1200 BC. It also reports that a 2015 burial near the palace, termed the “griffin warrior” burial by the excavating team, contained gold rings, bronze weapons, and other artifacts whose iconography combined Minoan and Mycenaean elements.

This source describes the so-called “Minos Ring,” rather than clearly identifying the object as the Ring of Nestor. Its abstract states that the ring’s find circumstances are examined through Spyridon Marinatos’ archives, that Spyridon Marinatos and Georg Karo considered the ring a forgery, and that new evidence presented in an appendix suggests that it is genuine.
